baseline_models.focus_anchor: The source phrase min Allah and the possessive title dhi al-ma'arij join the divine name at word 2 to the plural ma'arij at word 4.
baseline_models.mechanism: The worshipped one is named as possessor of multiple ways of upward movement, so vertical access is presented as an owned domain rather than as free space or a single ladder.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies worship and the worshipped one, making the named possessor the relational endpoint of the route system.
The branch supplies ascent upward and functions as the literal spatial action contained in the plural ma'arij.

changed_reading.before: A bare attribution to God followed by an honorific about height.
changed_reading.after: A source-linked title naming the worshipped one as owner of multiple concrete ways of ascent and therefore of access itself.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The plural ma'arij at word 4 can carry other root-local route images alongside straightforward ascent.
baseline_models.mechanism: Bending and turning aside to stop make the plural routes a network with changes of direction and stations; possession of them then implies control not only of destination but also of approach, delay, and passage.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies the worshipped one and gives the route network a devotional endpoint rather than leaving it as neutral geometry.
The branch supplies curving or turning and makes indirectness a possible property of the routes.
The branch supplies turning aside to stop or stay and functions as a possible station or pause within ascent.

changed_reading.before: The ma'arij are imagined as one straight, uninterrupted ladder.
changed_reading.after: The plural can evoke an administered access network whose routes bend and whose progress may include stations or delays.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding request, painful punishment, falling or fixed occurrence, and absence of a repelling force complete the focus fragment as provenance. The owner of upward routes is also the source of an event moving into the petitioner's world, producing a controlled counterflow between ascent and occurrence.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies Allah as the fixed divine name and makes min Allah an identified source rather than an abstract divine category.
The branch supplies upward ascent and forms the upward side of the model's directional contrast.
The branch supplies asking and requesting, making the opening event a demand whose answer is sourced by the focus phrase.
The branch supplies painful punishment and identifies what the request and source relation concern.
The branch supplies falling and becoming fixed, giving the threatened event both directional and irreversible force.
The branch supplies pushing away an unwelcome thing; its negation removes any counterforce to what comes from the possessor of ascents.

structural_cues: Ayat 70:1-3 form a continuous dependency chain: a request, its object and inevitability, the lack of a repeller, then min Allah and the title.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies request, punishment, occurrence, non-repulsion, provenance, and ascent; I infer a bidirectional vertical system governed from one source. Alternatively, waqi' may mark certainty without picturing literal downward motion.

changed_reading.before: Min Allah is an isolated statement of origin and ma'arij is a separate majestic title.
changed_reading.after: The phrase identifies the control point from which an unrepellable event arrives while all upward routes remain under the same possession.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah converts the nominal ma'arij into an enacted ascent by named classes of agents toward the pronominal endpoint. The title therefore describes an operating traffic system, not merely altitude.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies the worshipped one and functions as the endpoint toward whom the following traffic is directed.
The branch supplies upward ways and establishes the route inventory named by the title.
The branch supplies actual upward ascent and operationalizes the preceding plural routes as movement.
The branch supplies angels and identifies one class of agents that uses the routes.
The branch supplies spirit or the life-bearing spirit and identifies the paired second ascending agent without resolving its identity further.

structural_cues: The cognate verb opens 70:4 immediately after ma'arij, and the paired subjects are followed by ilayhi as a shared endpoint.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a cognate verb, two agents, and an endpoint; I infer that possession of the routes includes governance of their traffic. Alternatively, the title may denote rank while 70:4 independently describes ascent.

changed_reading.before: The ma'arij are static architecture or a general sign of loftiness.
changed_reading.after: They are active channels with traffic, users, direction, and a controlled endpoint.

context_deltas.mechanism: Enacted ascent is bound to an immense measured duration, then the same impending object is judged far by one viewpoint and near by another. The ma'arij become a scale-changing topology in which distance and duration depend on standpoint rather than ordinary human calibration.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies the upward routes whose scale is recalibrated by the context.
The branch supplies ascent in progress and connects route geometry to the following temporal measure.
The branch supplies a quantity that brings a thing to its limit and functions as the explicit calibration of the ascent-day.
The branch supplies remoteness as the human-side estimate of the event's distance.
The branch supplies nearness against remoteness and functions as the contrasting divine-side calibration.

structural_cues: Ayah 70:4 places the ascent in a day measured as fifty thousand years, while 70:6-7 reverse the perceiving subject around the same object pronoun.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ascent, a vast measure, and opposed far/near judgments; I read them as calibration of the ma'arij system. Alternatively, far and near may qualify only the punishment's timing, not the routes themselves.

changed_reading.before: The ascents are ordinary spatial distances that can be judged on a shared human scale.
changed_reading.after: The ascents organize a domain where spatial and temporal scale shifts with viewpoint, making human remoteness compatible with divine nearness.

context_deltas.mechanism: The high covering sky becomes a molten or sediment-like substance while solid raised mountains become soft dyed wool. Since the familiar vertical frame loses rigidity, the ma'arij read less like permanent physical stairs and more like an ordering of access that does not depend on stable cosmic materials.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies upward ways and anchors the model in the focus ayah's vertical architecture.
The branch supplies the sky as what is above and covering, establishing the ordinary upper frame that is transformed.
The branch supplies molten substances and sediments, converting the upper frame from firm structure into unstable material.
The branch supplies a high, gathered, solid mass and functions as the lower image of vertical permanence.
The branch supplies soft dyed wool and dissolves the mountain's solidity into pliable fibers.

structural_cues: The paired takunu...ka similes transform both upper sky and raised mountains in consecutive ayat.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies material transformations of the vertical world; I infer that the divine routes are not identical with that world's stable fabric. Alternatively, the similes may depict only the event's effects and say nothing about what ma'arij are made of.

changed_reading.before: The ma'arij are imagined as stairs built into a fixed sky-and-mountain cosmos.
changed_reading.after: They are a divinely possessed ordering of access that remains conceptually operative even when the visible vertical frame liquefies and softens.

context_deltas.mechanism: The long exception sequence begins with specific worship, makes it continuous, and immediately joins it to a fixed social due. Read against the worshipped possessor and the possible stopping-station image of arj, the plural ascents can function as practiced stations: recurrent devotion opens into durable obligation toward others.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies worship and the worshipped one, anchoring the later practices as approaches toward the named possessor.
The branch supplies a turn that includes stopping or staying and functions as the image of distinct, inhabited stations.
The branch supplies upward movement and makes the ordered practices a possible ascent rather than a flat list.
The branch supplies the specific act of worship and serves as the first practiced station in the exception sequence.
The branch supplies stillness and continuity, turning a momentary devotional act into sustained passage.
The branch supplies a fixed binding entitlement and makes social obligation the next durable station after prayer.

structural_cues: The exception at 70:22 opens a serial description through 70:34, framed by prayer near both its beginning and end.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies worship, continuity, a fixed due, and an ordered exception sequence; I map that sequence onto plural ascent-stations. Alternatively, it may describe protected character without intentionally glossing ma'arij.

changed_reading.before: The ascents belong only to a remote cosmic geography.
changed_reading.after: They may also name a lived pattern of recurrent worship and binding care, with ascent realized through sustained stations rather than escape from society.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later parallel title, Lord of the plural risings and plural settings, gives the earlier plural ascents a cosmic analogue. As light repeatedly rises and the sun repeatedly sets across horizons, ma'arij can denote manifold recurring trajectories rather than one vertical shaft.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies the fixed divine name that the later Lord-title redescribes.
The branch supplies ascent upward and forms the first plural trajectory set.
The branch supplies the rising of light from the east and functions as a visible recurring ascent analogue.
The branch supplies sunset and the west, completing the repeated horizon trajectory paired with rising.

structural_cues: Dhi al-ma'arij in 70:3 and bi-rabbi al-mashariqi wa-l-magharib in 70:40 are divine titles built from possessed plural spatial nouns.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies parallel divine titles and plural horizon motions; I infer that the later title gives a cyclic cosmic analogue for the earlier ascents. Alternatively, the titles may be independent assertions of dominion without mutual specification.

changed_reading.before: The ma'arij are a single exceptional ladder at one location.
changed_reading.after: They can be heard as a plurality of recurring cosmic trajectories distributed across changing horizons.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing scene directs rapid movement toward an erected marker, then reverses its vertical promise: eyes are lowered, an overpowering condition covers the crowd, and humiliation breaks them down. Against the opening possessor of true ascents, this becomes an anti-ascent in which directed speed toward a raised target ends in lowering rather than access.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies true upward movement and provides the opening vertical vector reversed by the close.
The branch supplies an erected boundary or target marker and functions as the crowd's conspicuous but non-ascending destination.
The branch supplies lowering and submission and turns the crowd's gaze downward after its rapid approach.
The branch supplies covering and overpowering and functions as the force that closes over the attempted movement.
The branch supplies breaking under domination and completes the anti-ascent as a collapse in status.

structural_cues: The branchless root و ف ض at 70:43 contributes only the supplied rushing syntax; it is not treated as branch evidence.
The final two ayat move from emergence and speed toward a raised marker to lowered sight and enveloping humiliation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a raised marker, rushing syntax, lowered eyes, overpowering, and humiliation; I infer that the close deliberately inverts the opening ascent. Alternatively, the scenes may contrast only in posture and not define access to the ma'arij.

changed_reading.before: The opening title contributes only an upward image with no corresponding negative choreography.
changed_reading.after: The title frames the close as a failed or counterfeit directed motion: speed toward what stands raised still ends in forced lowering because ascent belongs elsewhere.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the non-dominant س ل ل mapping of the context root س ء ل and its image of extracted paths, not the ordinary asking branch. It remains anchored to the focus source construction and the route-bearing ma'arij as a cross-root material analogy. Downstream prose should call it an exploratory echo of a question drawing out a response-path, never a lexical translation of sa'ala.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Min Allah supplies response provenance, while ma'arij supplies the route network to which the extracted-path image can attach.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies the fixed divine name and anchors the endpoint from which the requested matter is answered.
The branch supplies bending routes and gives the extracted-path image a focus-level spatial attachment.
The split-mapped branch supplies paths drawn or pulled out and functions as a material analogy for the request exposing a route of response.

changed_reading.before: The opening question merely names the topic answered by a static source phrase.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the request can be pictured as drawing out a latent route along which the matter is disclosed from the possessor of routes.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the watering-interval branch of ع ر ج is lexically remote from ma'arij as ascents. It remains root-anchored, and the immediately measured day supplies a real temporal cue for a cadence analogy. Downstream prose should say the routes may evoke scheduled or alternating access, not redefine ma'arij as camel watering.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The plural ma'arij at word 4 carries a root-local interval image that can interact with the measured duration immediately following the focus.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies an alternating watering interval and functions only as a cadence analogy within the plural routes.
The branch supplies a duration of time and gives the cadence analogy an explicit temporal frame.
The branch supplies a bounded measure and functions as the scheduling or interval constraint on the imagined cadence.

changed_reading.before: The ascents are purely spatial and continuously available.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, the plural ascents may also evoke measured, recurrent, or alternating windows of passage.

strongest_changes: The immediate context turns the fragment into the source statement for an unrepellable occurring punishment, placing downward arrival and upward ascent under one control point.
The cognate ascent by angels and spirit operationalizes ma'arij as trafficked routes, while measure and far/near viewpoints make their scale observer-dependent.
The closing rush toward a raised marker followed by lowered eyes and humiliation creates a strong anti-ascent that answers the opening title.
summary.what_was_special: The plural ma'arij supported several coexisting mechanisms: governed traffic, changing scale, nonmaterial architecture, practiced stations, horizon cycles, and a closing vertical reversal. Split-root and interval images also yielded contained outliers without replacing the ordinary ascent sense.
remaining_uncertainties: Waqi' may express inevitable occurrence rather than literal falling, which would weaken the bidirectional spatial model but not the provenance model.
The ethical sequence and the plural horizon title may resonate with ma'arij without intentionally explaining it.
Curving, stopping, extracted-path, and cadence images are root-level activations whose lexical force in ma'arij remains exploratory.
